Subject: Private deployment patching — version pinning & rollback questions

Hi Karthik,

We want to align on the plan for the upcoming patch on our private Redwood deployment (VPC, customer-managed control plane). A few items we need clarity on before we approve a maintenance window:

- If you push a quantized/runtime patch, can we pin nodes to exact image tags (no auto-promote)?
- What are typical maintenance windows and expected total downtime per region for a rolling patch?
- How do you handle rollback if a model runtime/quantization regression is discovered post-rollout?
- We also need a quick list of security/compliance steps (KMS rekeying, audit log retention) that will be touched during the change.

Can you send a proposed schedule and the rollback runbook? Attaching our internal blackout windows for reference (not included in this thread).

Thanks,
Maya Singh
Head of Platform Ops | AtlasEdge
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment patching — version pinning & rollback questions

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. We've put together an initial plan and a couple of artifacts (patch matrix + high-level playbook). See attached: patch_matrix_v1.xlsx, maintenance_playbook.pdf.

High level answers first:
- Version pinning: yes — we will deploy with explicit image tags (example: redwood/inference:v2.4.1-redwood-202609). No automatic promotion.
- Maintenance window: our recommended baseline is a 3-hour window per region for full rollout and verification; expected *service-impactful* disruption per node is minimized via rolling canaries (typically <30s for inference handoff; see notes). Total perceived client-side latency spike depends on your SLOs and prefix-caching.
- Rollback: we support fast rollback to the prior image tag (v2.3.9 in our test matrix) and automatic traffic steering back to the fallback model variant. Rollback runbook is being prepared.
- Security/compliance: we'll coordinate KMS access, provide audit logs (retention window we recommend is 90 days for the maintenance window), and rotate ephemeral keys only if requested.

Can we target a tentative window next Monday/Tue (Sep 20-21 UTC nights)? I want to run a technical review with Priyom and Jasmine to validate the plan and finalize the runbook.

Karthik
Account Lead — Private Deployments

Internal — looping you both in to validate network and rollback mechanics for AtlasEdge's private deployment. Quick context: customer wants explicit version pinning, clear rollback, and compliance notes. Key asks below — please reply inline with ETA and any blockers.

1) Version pinning semantics: confirm we can pin both runtime container tags and model artifact tag, and that we won't auto-promote any sidecar (metrics/exporter) changes.
2) Rolling strategy: propose canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% per AZ, with health checks at each stage. Provide expected durations per phase.
3) DB/migration risk: do we need any schema migrations or stateful changes? If yes, include pre/post-snapshot steps.
4) Network ACLs & private CIDR changes: AtlasEdge may ask for short ACLs during switchover — confirm if we need to coordinate with their network team or if we can use existing NAT/peering flows.
5) Rollback runbook: provide step-by-step timed actions and exact kubectl or orchestration commands we will run.

Attachments: patch_matrix_v1.xlsx (customer-facing matrix) and maintenance_playbook.pdf (high-level timeline).

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: AtlasEdge patch orchestration - technical review

Karthik / Jasmine — technical runbook (summary) below; full runbook attached as rollback_runbook.md. I'll add timed checkpoints to the shared Drive doc.

- Version pinning: Confirmed. We'll pin 3 artifacts: runtime image tag (redwood/inference:v2.4.1-redwood-202609), model artifact (model-v3.1-q8), and quantization metadata. No auto-promote on sidecars.

- Rollout phases & durations (per region):
  * Canary (5% nodes) — 15min warm + 15min traffic verification = 30min
  * 25% stage — 20min warm + 20min verification = 40min
  * 50% stage — 30min warm + 30min verification = 60min
  * 100% stage — 30min warm + 60min verification = 90min
  Estimated total: ~3h (including buffer checkpoints).

- State / DB migrations: NONE for this release. We only change runtime and model artifacts. No schema or DB writes expected. We will, however, snapshot PVs for the logging state and take a consistent KV cache snapshot prior to canary start (customer-provided snapshot API recommended).

- Networking: No CIDR changes required. We will ask AtlasEdge SRE to temporarily allow a short ACL rule for health-check ports (TCP 443 and 8080) from our canary CIDR for 45 minutes. After rollout, ACLs can be reverted. We'll provide exact rule JSON for IaC.

- Rollback commands (high-level):
  1) set-image deployment/inference redwood/inference:v2.3.9 && kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference
  2) switch traffic via service annotation to fallback variant
  3) monitor 5m; if healthy, continue verification; otherwise escalate to on-call.

- Observability: collector will retain tracing for 7 days; we will attach per-request token traces for a 6-hour window post-rollout for immediate regression debugging.

Attaching: rollback_runbook.md

Priyom
Senior SRE — Serving Runtime

Quick security/compliance notes for AtlasEdge:

- KMS: We will not rotate customer master keys during this patch. If AtlasEdge requests key rotation, it must be scheduled as a separate maintenance window.
- Ephemeral keys: session-level keys (for agent provisioning) will be regenerated for canaries only. We will log key creation and deletion events to the audit trail.
- Audit logs: we'll snapshot audit logs for the 7-day window encompassing the rollout. Retention: provide a 90-day export if needed (we can upload to their S3).
- SOC2 evidence: include the maintenance_playbook.pdf and rollback_runbook.md in the evidence bundle. Recommend a 2-hour buffer before and after the maintenance window to cover any security snapshotting.

Also: request that AtlasEdge enable cross-account read for our support account for the specific bucket path during the 24-hour post-maintenance period.

-Jasmine
